question: The term 'Sangam' refers to which of the following? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: A Tamil dynasty
A literary assembly of Tamil scholars
A type of Tamil poetry
South Indian religious texts
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A literary assembly of Tamil scholars

Explanation:
The term 'Sangam' in ancient Tamil literature refers to a literary assembly of Tamil scholars. These assemblies were held in three periods (Sangam period) from approximately 300 BCE to 300 CE. The first Sangam was held in Madurai, the second in Kapāṭapuram, and the third again in Madurai. During these assemblies, poets and scholars composed Tamil poems and texts, which were later compiled. The early part of Tamil literature is called Sangam literature, which includes collections like Ettuthokai and Pattupattu. These assemblies were crucial for preserving Tamil culture and language, and they acted as academies for literary criticism and patronage. The Sangam period is considered the golden age of Tamil literature, with works like Tolkāppiyam (grammar) and Silappadikaram (epic) originating from this tradition.

☛ Where was the first Sangam assembly held? → Madurai
☛ How many major collections are in Sangam literature? → Two: Ettuthokai and Pattupattu
☛ What was the time span of the Sangam period? → 300 BCE to 300 CE
☛ What was the main function of Tamil Sangam? → Evaluation and preservation of literary works
☛ When and where was the third Sangam held? → 3rd century CE in Madurai

question: According to Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan traveller to India during the Delhi Sultanate, the method of postal system in which the royal horses were used to transfer packages, is called: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dawa
Uluq
Mansabdari
Ikat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uluq

Explanation:
According to Ibn Battuta's travelogue 'Rihla', the postal system of the Delhi Sultanate was called 'Uluq'. It primarily used royal horses for transferring packages and messages. Relay stations were established at regular intervals (a few miles apart) where fresh horses were kept ready, enabling rapid communication. Foot runners were also employed alongside. This system ensured swift delivery of official correspondence and parcels, playing a vital role in maintaining administrative control over the vast empire. It was an efficient network that connected the sultanate's key regions, facilitating quick decision-making and surveillance.

☛ Ibn Battuta's travelogue → Rihla

☛ Location of relay stations in Uluq → Every few miles

question: During the rule of which of the following Mughal rulers did Sunnis and Shias meet in one mosque and Christians and Jews in one church to pray, thus following the principle of 'universal peace' (sulh-i kul)?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Jahangir
Babar
Humayun
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
Mughal emperor Akbar adopted a policy of religious tolerance in his empire known as sulh-i kul (universal peace). During his reign, he established the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri, where scholars of different religions discussed theological matters. According to the historian Abul Fazl, Akbar arranged a place where Sunnis and Shias could pray together in one mosque, and Christians and Jews in one church, in line with the principle of sulh-i kul. This reflected his commitment to interfaith harmony. Akbar also founded a syncretic religion called Din-i Ilahi, though it did not last long. His policies fostered communal harmony and strengthened the empire's unity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Name of Akbar's religious policy → Sulh-i kul
☛ Location of Ibadat Khana → Fatehpur Sikri
☛ Religion founded by Akbar → Din-i Ilahi
☛ Work authored by Abul Fazl → Ain-i Akbari
☛ Akbar's reign period → 1556-1605
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस मुगल शासक के शासनकाल में सुन्नियों और शियाओं ने एक मस्जिद में और ईसाइयों और यहूदियों ने एक चर्च में प्रार्थना करने के लिए मुलाकात की, इस प्रकार 'सार्वभौमिक शांति' (सुल्ह-ए-कुल) के सिद्धांत का पालन किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
मुगल सम्राट अकबर ने अपने साम्राज्य में धार्मिक सहिष्णुता की नीति अपनाई, जिसे सुल्ह-ए-कुल (सार्वभौमिक शांति) कहा जाता है। इसी नीति के तहत उनके शासनकाल में इबादत खाना (पूजा गृह) स्थापित किया गया, जहाँ विभिन्न धर्मों के विद्वान एक साथ धार्मिक चर्चा करते थे। प्रसिद्ध इतिहासकार अबुल फजल के अनुसार, अकबर ने फतेहपुर सीकरी में एक स्थान बनाया जहाँ सुन्नी और शिया एक मस्जिद में, तथा ईसाई और यहूदी एक चर्च में एक साथ प्रार्थना कर सकते थे, जो सुल्ह-ए-कुल के सिद्धांत को दर्शाता है। अकबर ने दीन-ए-इलाही नामक एक नया धर्म भी चलाया, लेकिन यह अल्पकालिक रहा। उनकी इस नीति ने साम्राज्य में सांप्रदायिक सद्भाव को बढ़ावा दिया।

question: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and which Indian power?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Mughals
Rajputs
British
Marathas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marathas

Explanation:
The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas. It took place on January 14, 1761, and is considered one of the largest battles in India. The Maratha forces were led by Sadashivrao Bhau, while Abdali's army included Afghans and Rohillas. The Marathas lost due to internal divisions, lack of supplies, and Abdali's superior strategy. This battle significantly weakened the Maratha Empire and paved the way for the rise of British power in India.

question: In the Pallava administration, which was the smallest administrative unit directly managed by local self-governing assemblies? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Nadu
Mandala
Ur
Kottam
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ur

Explanation:
In the Pallava administration, Ur was the smallest administrative unit directly managed by local self-governing assemblies. It referred to a village or a small settlement. The Pallava system comprised three main territorial divisions: Kottam (district), Nadu (administrative subdivision), and Ur (village). The state was divided into several Kottams for administrative convenience, which were further subdivided into Nadus. The Ur assemblies oversaw local matters such as land management, tax collection, and judicial functions. These autonomous assemblies enabled local control over resources and dispute resolution. Thus, the Ur system ensured effective governance at the grassroots level.

☛ What was the local assembly in Pallava villages called? → Ur Sabha
☛ What area was managed by the Ur assembly? → A village
☛ What did 'Nadu' mean in Pallava administration? → Administrative subdivision
☛ What modern division corresponds to a Kottam? → District

question: From the 11th through the 18th centuries, what type of literature was the most prominent in medieval India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Theatrical historical performances
Devotional poetry
Elaborate philosophical discussions
Specialised scientific writings
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Devotional poetry

Explanation:
During medieval India (11th to 18th centuries), the Bhakti movement flourished, and devotional poetry became the most prominent literary form. Saints like Kabir, Tulsidas, Mirabai, Surdas, Nanak, and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu composed verses expressing love and devotion to God in local languages. This literature was simple and accessible to common people, challenging social norms and caste hierarchies. Devotional poetry not only fostered religious awakening but also contributed to the development of regional languages such as Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, and Bengali. While other forms like theatrical performances and philosophical discussions existed, none matched the widespread appeal and impact of devotional poetry, which remains a significant cultural heritage of India.

☛ What language did medieval devotional poetry use? → Regional vernaculars (Hindi, Marathi, Bengali)
☛ Who wrote Ramcharitmanas? → Tulsidas (16th century)
☛ What is the collection of Guru Nanak's compositions? → Guru Granth Sahib
☛ What is the central theme of devotional poetry? → Love and devotion to God

question: During the Mughal period, the Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by _____. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)

Shah Jahan
Akbar
Aurangzeb
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
The Ain-i-Dahsala system was introduced by the Mughal emperor Akbar. It was a crucial part of the land revenue system developed under the guidance of Raja Todar Mal. Under this system, land was measured and assessed based on the average production over ten years, and the revenue was collected from farmers in cash at a fixed rate. This system was fairer and more transparent for the farmers and provided financial stability to the Mughal Empire. The Ain-i-Dahsala is considered a major reform in Mughal revenue administration.

question: Market control under Alauddin Khilji aimed mainly to ________. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 2)

This market control was crucial for sustaining his military campaigns and maintaining political stability.

question: The governor of a province (bhukti) in the Pala and Pratihara empire was called:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Rashtrapati
Uparika
Visayapati
Koshtapala
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uparika

Explanation:
In the administrative system of the Pala and Pratihara empires, a province was called a 'bhukti'. The governor appointed to administer this bhukti was known as 'Uparika'. The main duties of an Uparika included maintaining law and order, collecting taxes, and ensuring loyalty to the central authority. This position was appointed by the central power and oversaw several districts (vishayas), each administered by a Vishayapati. While Rashtrapati was a higher rank sometimes in charge of provinces in other empires, and Koshtapala was a treasurer, the Uparika specifically governed the bhukti. Thus, the term Uparika was used for the provincial governor in the Pala-Pratihara administration.

question: In which of the following sections of Akbarnama does Abul Fazal discuss Akbar's administration, household, army, revenue and geography of his empire? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 1)

in both the second and third sections

Explanation:
Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in three volumes. The first volume deals with Akbar's ancestors and the early part of his reign. The second volume describes the events of Akbar's reign. Hence, the third section focuses on administration, household, army, revenue, and geography.

question: The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict among the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and which southern Indian dynasty? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Rashtrakutas
Cholas
Satavahanas
Pallavas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rashtrakutas

Explanation:
The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict among the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas for control over Kannauj, which was a strategic and cultural center in early medieval India. This struggle lasted from the 8th to the 10th century and significantly drained the resources of all three powers. The Rashtrakutas were a Deccan dynasty based at Manyakheta, while the Palas ruled Bengal (east) and the Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled Rajasthan-Gujarat (west). The conflict centered on Kannauj because of its prestige and location in the Gangetic plains. The continuous warfare led to the weakening of all three dynasties, paving the way for other powers like the Chandellas and Ghaznavids.

question_hi: त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष गुर्जर-प्रतिहार, पाल और किस दक्षिण भारतीय राजवंश के बीच एक लम्बा संघर्ष था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: राष्ट्रकूट
चोल
सातवाहन
पल्लव
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रकूट

Explanation:
त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष (Tripartite Struggle) उत्तर भारत की सत्ता के लिए तीन शक्तियों के बीच हुआ था: गुर्जर-प्रतिहार, पाल और राष्ट्रकूट। यह संघर्ष लगभग 200 वर्षों (8वीं से 10वीं शताब्दी) तक चला और इसका मुख्य कारण कन्नौज पर नियंत्रण प्राप्त करना था, जो तत्कालीन भारत का सामरिक एवं सांस्कृतिक केंद्र था। इस संघर्ष में राष्ट्रकूट दक्षिण भारतीय राजवंश था जिसकी राजधानी मान्यखेत थी। पाल वंश बंगाल क्षेत्र (पूर्व), गुर्जर-प्रतिहार राजस्थान-गुजरात (पश्चिम) और राष्ट्रकूट दक्कन क्षेत्र (दक्षिण) से था। यह तीनों कन्नौज पर अधिकार जमाने के लिए सदियों लड़ते रहे, जिससे उनका पारस्परिक दुर्बलता हुई।
